contraceptive-pill-usage-in-great-britai.precis: Contraceptive pill usage in Great Britain fell drastically in last decade, research finds, according to The Guardian. Survey published in Lancet reveals ‘hormonal hesitancy’ on the rise – with implants and injections also increasingly spurned The number of young women using hormonal contraception fell drastically in the past decade, with social media fuelling the “hormonal hesitancy” phenomenon. New findings from the fourth National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4), published in The Lancet, found that almost one in five women in Great Britain at risk of unintended pregnancy were not using effective contraception.
